title: Manila Bay (the water west of the 1899 shore)
how_read: Not read from a map: the area between the traced shore and the sheet's edge.

title: The 1899 shore, Vitas canal to Malate
how_read: Read point by point from gridded crops of the scan.

title: The shore north of Vitas and south of Pasay
link_label: The Signal Corps map: the bay shore (Library of Congress)
how_read: Read from the Signal Corps map and slid to meet the shore of the better maps (8 m in the north, to the engineer map; 236 m in the south, to the 1898 plan).

title: The jetty and the north mole at the mouth of the Pasig
how_read: Read point by point from gridded crops of the scan.

title: Pasig River, the mouth to below Santa Ana
how_read: The map's blue water tint separated by colour inside the inked banks and vectorised by program; gaps under lettering closed and leaks cut by hand.

title: Pasig River above Santa Ana
link_label: The Signal Corps map: Santa Ana to San Pedro Macati (Library of Congress)
how_read: A centre line read from the Signal Corps map and slid 140 m to meet the engineer map's river.

title: San Juan River
how_read: Centre line read point by point.

title: Lagoons and fish ponds behind the Tondo beach
how_read: The water tint separated by colour and vectorised by program; ponds, dykes and open water are not told apart.

title: Moat of the Walled City
how_read: The water tint around the walls separated by colour and vectorised by program.

title: Walls of the Walled City (Intramuros)
how_read: The main wall in 43 points; bastions, gates and outworks simplified away.

title: Manila and Dagupan Railway
how_read: Read point by point; tied across the track to today's line, which keeps the 1892 right of way.

title: Main roads
how_read: Thirteen roads read point by point. Six carry a name lettered on the map; the others are described, not named. Roads north of the city are low confidence.

title: Blockhouses 1 to 12
how_read: The blockhouse symbols. Numbers 2 to 6 are low confidence: no control point lies near them.

title: Streets, blocks, dykes and field lines: the engineer map's own ink
how_read: Every dark ink line of the map, separated from the scan by a program, thinned to centre lines and vectorised; small separate marks (most lettering) dropped by size. Not checked line by line: a few letters that touch a line are in it, and so are small field works drawn after 4 February. The long American trench line of 5 to 28 February was cut out.

title: Esteros, creeks and ponds
how_read: The map's blue water wash over the whole sheet, separated by colour and vectorised by a program, less the water of the layers above. Creeks are cut where the wash fades or lettering covers them.

title: Insurgent field works by blockhouses 1 and 2
how_read: The legend's "Insurg." mark (a row of humps), read from an enlarged crop. The map draws these works only here.

title: The shore from Malate to Pasay
how_read: Read from crops of the 1898 plan and checked by laying the picks back on the scan. South of Malate the plan is a hand-drawn strip: it is slid to today's F. B. Harrison Street and its Pasay crossing (up to 287 m), and may still be 100 m out.

title: Calle Real, Malate to Pasay
how_read: The double-line road nearest the shore, read from crops of the 1898 plan. Placed as the shore of this map is.

title: Blockhouses 13 and 14
how_read: Two works on the old Spanish line with 13 and 14 written beside them in pencil on the Yale copy. Placed as the shore of this map is; the Signal Corps map puts blockhouse 14 about 270 m away.

title: Roads, field lines, marsh and old works south of Malate: the 1898 plan's own ink
how_read: Every dark ink line of the 1898 plan south of where the engineer map stops, separated from the scan by a program and vectorised; lettering, trees and houses dropped by size. It is the ground of 1898 and includes the trenches of that August. Not checked line by line.

title: The city in fine detail: the 1898 plan's own ink
how_read: Every dark mark of the 1898 plan of the city, kept as printed with the paper made clear (pipeline/recon/manila_1898_ink.py), and laid on the ground by the plan's fit to the engineer map (half the matched points within 5.7 m). Shown from the closer zooms. Streets, blocks, public buildings, street names and building numbers; the title and keys left out. The city of 1898; not checked mark by mark.
notes: A picture (playbacks/manila/manila-1898-ink.webp, and two smaller sizes), not lines: tap it for this record. Added 22 Nov 2026 so that zooming in shows more of the city.

title: Street and block edges the 1898 plan also draws: the engineer map's ink
how_read: The lines of the layer above that the 1898 plan of the city draws too (seven points in ten within 16 m of its ink): 2,483 of 6,614. At the closest zooms they give way to the plan's finer drawing, so a street edge is not drawn twice.
notes: Split from the linework layer on 22 Nov 2026; the lines themselves are unchanged.
